newsitem.title: USA: US stocks to open lower after trade gap swells.
newsitem.headline: US stocks to open lower after trade gap swells.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open mixed after the September trade deficit rose much more than expected.
"My guess is, with bonds and futures getting hit (by the data), it's got to put some pressure on equity prices," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherfood Brown and Catherwood.

The U.S. international trade deficit unexpectedly swelled 10.1 percent to a whopping $11.34 billion in September, which also sent economists scrambling to cut third-quarter Gross Domestic Product growth estimates.
"It's surprising because the Commerce Department estimated exports would have been up. They were down 1.4 (percent)," said Donald Maude, chief U.S. economist at Scotia Capital Markets.
The Long bond fell after the news by 10/32 to yield 6.46 percent.
